Subject: Sequencing the MAP — proposed commit waterfall and eval milestones

Sarah / Carlos — great to meet last week. Per our conversation I've attached a first-pass MAP and a lightweight commit waterfall for the pilot. High level:

- 4-week evaluation (pilot) for feature experimentation: 100k tokens / month baseline for eval.
- Post-eval ramp (month 2–3): staged commit to 400k tokens/mo with automatic bulk discounts at 250k and 400k thresholds.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up with lookback to committed volumes for price protection during ramp.

Key asks from our side: confirm the evaluation success criteria (latency SLA on P50/P95, accuracy thresholds on the intent classifier test-suite) and whether OliveTech can accept a quarterly true-up and a price-protection clause tied to committed volumes.

Attachments: OliveTech-MAP-v1.pdf, proposed-sow-commit-waterfall.xlsx

Next steps: if you confirm acceptance of these milestones I will loop in legal to produce a short SOW + redlines doc for your procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week to walk through sequencing.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0172

Aditya — thanks, this looks promising. A few clarifying points from procurement before we bring legal fully in:

1) Can the evaluation volume be counted against the initial commit if we convert? We prefer eval usage to reduce our initial ramp risk.
2) Price protection: we need to understand how an early conversion affects the discount thresholds and whether the quarterly true-up could create retroactive charges without a cap.
3) Definitions: we need a clear definition of "billable token" vs. "inference token", and whether model variants (quantized vs full FP16) are treated the same for pricing.

Sarah and I are available Thu 10/8 at 10am PT to discuss. Can you and your team include someone from product/technical to confirm the usage definitions?

Thanks,
Carlos

Carlos / Sarah — good notes. Quick responses inline and attaching an updated draft SOW with more explicit sequencing and a definitions annex.

- Eval counting toward commit: yes — if OliveTech elects to convert to a committed plan within 60 days of the evaluation window close, up to 50% of eval usage can be credited against the initial commit. We propose that credit flow only at the first true-up to keep invoicing simple.
- Price protection & caps: we can offer price protection across the first 12 months post-commit with a cap on retroactive charges equal to 10% of the quarter's invoice (this is negotiable).
- Billable token definition: billable token = tokens sent + tokens returned by the model; we will include a clear mapping for different model variants. Quantized variants that are Redwood-provided model variants will be considered functionally equivalent for billing unless a higher-throughput variant is requested.

Attached: redlines-10-12-26.docx includes the proposed language for the credit, cap, and definitions annex.

Internally, Lauren/Priyom — please review the proposed 50% eval-credit, 12-month price-protection window, and the 10% retro cap. Neha, can legal validate whether the wording is acceptable from a risk perspective or suggest alternate language (we want to avoid an uncapped clawback).

Can we aim to have a legal-ready draft by 10/12 so OliveTech can route it the same week?

Thanks,
Aditya

[Attachment stubs: proposed-sow-commit-waterfall.xlsx, redlines-10-12-26.docx]

Subject: Re: Sequencing the MAP — proposed commit waterfall and eval milestones

Team — reviewed the proposed language and drafting notes. High-level comments for negotiation with OliveTech Legal: 

1) Eval credit mechanics: the 50% credit toward initial commit is reasonable, but we should tie the credit to verified usage logs and agree on an audit process. Suggest adding: "credit applied after reconciliation of evaluation logs between parties within 30 days of evaluation close."

2) Price protection window: 12 months is fine, but request we limit the protection to committed SKUs / model families and exclude special promotional pricing. Add explicit carve-outs for overage charges incurred from third-party add-ons.

3) Retroactive cap: a 10% cap is acceptable, but define the cap on an invoice-by-invoice basis and include a monthly smoothing clause to avoid a single-quarter spike. Proposed language: "retroactive adjustments shall not exceed 10% of the individual quarterly invoice and, if exceeded, may be amortized over the following two billing cycles at customer election."

4) Definitions annex: expand the token definition to include examples (chat vs. embedding vs streaming scenarios) and call out how cached / prefix tokens are treated for billing. This will reduce back-and-forth with their team.

Action items: I'll produce suggested redline text for 10/15. Aditya — please confirm you want me to send the redline directly to OliveTech legal or you prefer we route via procurement (Carlos).

-Neha
General Counsel | Redwood Inference
